Kennedy Space Center LC-39A, 2024-10-14. The largest spacecraft NASA has ever launched for a planetary mission — 6065 kg with 100-m² solar arrays (the largest interplanetary photovoltaic system at the time). Europa Clipper is the first mission dedicated specifically to characterising the habitability of one of Jupiter's icy moons.
Falcon Heavy second stage delivers Clipper at C3 41.7 km²/s² onto a Mars-gravity-assist trajectory.
2025-03-01. Mars MGA bends the trajectory toward an Earth re-encounter, adding the energy chemical propulsion alone couldn't deliver economically.
2026-12-03. EGA accelerates Clipper outbound to Jupiter, closing the 5.5-year cruise.
2030-04-11. Clipper begins the final approach to Jupiter for orbital insertion.

Multi-engine burn places Clipper into a highly elliptical Jupiter orbit, with apoapsis carefully timed to keep the spacecraft outside the worst of Jupiter's radiation belts. The orbital tour will execute 49 close Europa flybys over four years — passing within 25 km of Europa's surface on the closest passes. Each flyby strips Europa's ice-shell secrets one swath at a time: REASON ice-penetrating radar profiles the shell, MASPEX mass spectrometer samples plume material if any, E-THEMIS thermal imager finds active geysers.
First mission dedicated to characterising the habitability of an icy moon; largest spacecraft NASA has ever launched for a planetary mission (6065 kg, 100-m² solar arrays)

Europa Clipper goes to Jupiter to study Europa — a 3,121-km icy moon believed to harbour a global liquid-water ocean beneath a 15-25 km ice shell, the most accessible potentially-habitable environment in the solar system. Launched 2024-10-14 on a Falcon Heavy at C3 41.7. A Mars gravity assist in March 2025 bent the trajectory toward Earth; an Earth gravity assist 2026-12 delivers the final push outward; arrives Jupiter 2030-04-11 for orbit insertion. The orbital tour executes 49 close Europa flybys over four years — passing within 25 km of Europa's surface on the closest passes, designed to map the entire moon while limiting the spacecraft's dose in Jupiter's brutal radiation belts. Instruments: REASON ice-penetrating radar, MASPEX mass spectrometer (samples plume material if any), E-THEMIS thermal imager (finds active geysers), magnetometer + plasma instruments confirm ocean depth from induced magnetic response.
Orbit-insertion burn. 49 Europa flybys over 4 years follow.
